skill.name: debugging-websocket-issues
skill.description: Guides debugging for Node.js WebSocket frame errors, upgrade-handler conflicts, compression mismatches, and raw frame inspection.
skill.summary: Debug Node.js WebSocket frame errors caused by upgrade routing, compression, or raw HTTP responses.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced TypeScript examples, and WebSocket error text. I found no shell execution, outbound network behavior, prompt injection, or system reconnaissance. One low-severity semantic concern remains because the raw frame debugging example can log payload bytes.

remediation.issue: Raw frame byte logging may expose message content.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to use byte logging only in controlled debugging sessions, redact sensitive data, and remove the hook after diagnosis.

content.value_statement: WebSocket frame errors can hide upgrade routing conflicts, compression mismatches, or raw HTTP on upgraded sockets. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through targeted checks for Node.js ws servers.
actual_capabilities: Explains common causes of invalid WebSocket frame headers in Node.js applications.
Identifies multiple WebSocketServer upgrade listener conflicts.
Shows how noServer routing can separate WebSocket paths.
Guides raw frame inspection for HTTP text and RSV1 bits.
Lists verification checks after changing upgrade and compression settings.
limitations: Focused on Node.js ws style servers and HTTP upgrade handling.
Does not inspect live traffic or run diagnostics by itself.
Requires access to server logs, client errors, or captured frame bytes.
Examples may need adaptation for frameworks, proxies, and managed hosts.

use_cases.title: Backend Incident Debugging
use_cases.description: Trace invalid frame header errors from client symptoms to upgrade-handler conflicts or compression mismatches.

use_cases.title: Platform WebSocket Reviews
use_cases.description: Review shared HTTP servers that route several WebSocket paths through one application entry point.

use_cases.title: AI-Assisted Code Diagnosis
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a structured checklist for diagnosing Node.js ws failures.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a known client error.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why my WebSocket client reports an invalid frame header. Ask for the smallest set of server and client details needed.

prompt_templates.title: Find Upgrade Conflicts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of server routing behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WebSocket server setup for multiple upgrade handlers or conflicting WebSocketServer instances. Focus on likely causes of raw HTTP on the socket.

prompt_templates.title: Plan noServer Routing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from automatic server attachment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from multiple server-attached WebSocket handlers to one upgrade router using noServer mode. Include verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Captured Frames
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis with logs and frame bytes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these WebSocket logs and captured first bytes. Determine whether the failure points to compression, raw HTTP, or another frame mismatch.

output_examples.input: My client reports RSV1 must be clear right after connecting to a WebSocket path.
output_examples.output: Likely causes include duplicate upgrade handlers or a compression mismatch. Check whether raw HTTP appears in the first bytes before changing payload handling.

output_examples.input: Two WebSocket paths work alone, but one fails when both are enabled.
output_examples.output: This pattern points to competing upgrade listeners. Use one upgrade router and route each path to the matching WebSocket server.

output_examples.input: The frame bytes start with the characters for HTTP.
output_examples.output: The client is receiving an HTTP response after the upgrade. Inspect non-matching handlers, rejected paths, and any abort response written to the socket.

best_practices: Start with upgrade routing before assuming payload corruption.
Confirm compression settings on both client and server before changing defaults.
Remove byte logging after local diagnosis and keep sensitive payloads out of logs.
anti_patterns: Running multiple automatic WebSocket servers on one HTTP server without a single router.
Leaving raw frame byte logging enabled in shared or production environments.
Treating every RSV1 error as compression without checking for HTTP text.

faq.question: Does this skill run network tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to apply with user-provided logs and code.

faq.question: Which WebSocket libraries does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Node.js ws patterns, especially WebSocketServer, noServer routing, and HTTP upgrade handling.

faq.question: Can it fix production incidents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify likely causes and verification steps, but users must apply and test changes.

faq.question: Why does it recommend noServer routing?
faq.answer: noServer routing lets one upgrade handler choose the correct WebSocket server and avoids competing listeners.

faq.question: Is perMessageDeflate always unsafe?
faq.answer: No. It can be valid when both sides negotiate it correctly. The skill treats it as one possible cause to verify.

faq.question: Do I need captured frame bytes?
faq.answer: No, but first-byte evidence can separate raw HTTP responses from compression or protocol mismatch issues.
